_about: IBM's Multi-PNA+EU on the 16 held-out transactions the published finance MLP and compact GNN are checked on, with the neighbourhood its loader sampled for them, written by scripts/train/ibm_multignn/export_for_browser.py.
protocol_note: Neighbours sampled from the whole test graph, as IBM's loader draws them: a neighbourhood includes transactions later than the one scored.

view.about: Each forward edge's row in the time-ordered file (its batch of 2,048 is the row divided by 2,048) and its time in seconds from the corpus's first transfer, the reach (the furthest a fit-window row sees to the end of its batch), and per seed what the model read, as scripts/train/ibm_multignn/neighbourhood.py defines it.

expected.decision_threshold_note: the laundering probability at which F1 peaks on the validation window, from precise_bn.py's probabilities (BatchNorm statistics recomputed on the fit window)
expected.note: Accuracy on 16 rows, half of them laundering, at the validation-tuned threshold: it shows the model running on the record's inputs, not how well it ranks.

per_row.margin_is: p(class 1) minus the decision threshold; class 1 at or above 0
per_row.note: From ONNX Runtime's outputs on this file's inputs, by the page's rule.

modifications: Not the published transaction rows: the 16 rows of the held-out temporal test window that the published MLP's weights carry as fixtures, half of them laundering, with the subgraph IBM's Multi-GNN loader samples around them under this protocol. Re-encoded as IBM's format script encodes the corpus (scripts/train/ibm_multignn/format_amlworld.py: integer account, currency and payment-format codes, seconds from the first day), with port numbers and ego ids added and every edge feature scaled by each window's own statistics, as IBM's loader scales them, stored as float32.
attribution: IBM, Transactions for Anti Money Laundering (AML), HI-Small (Altman et al., NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks); model: IBM/Multi-GNN (Egressy et al., AAAI 2024), Apache-2.0
